statement: Champions of the Future (COTF) is a kart racing competition organised by the RGMMC Group and sanctioned by FIA Karting (CIK-FIA).
Founded in 2020, COTF is one of 11 competitions on the international kart racing calendar in CIK-FIA classes.
The championship initially consisted of a two-round series in OK and OK-Junior (OK-J) with single-round finals in KZ2 and 60 Mini.
The championship has since expanded to all eight CIK-FIA classes across the Euro Series (OK, OK-J), Shifters (KZ, KZ2, KZ2-M), and Academy Program (OK-N, OKN-J, 60 Mini).
The Academy Program is supported by F1 Academy.
COTF hosted the one-off Winter Series at Franciacorta in 2022.
COTF is set to expand to national series in 2026, hosting a British title with Motorsport UK, an Emirati title, a Macanese title, and an American title.
The Euro Series and Shifters events traditionally take place in the two weeks prior to a World or European Championship round at the same circuit.
Nikita Bedrin was a notable former champion in OK in 2020.
Arvid Lindblad was a notable former champion in OK-J in 2020.
Rafael Câmara was a notable former champion in OK in 2021.
Freddie Slater was a notable former champion in OK-J in 2021.
Alex Powell was a notable former champion in OK in 2023.
Dries Van Langendonck was a notable former champion in OK-J in 2024.
Luna Fluxá (2024, OK-N) is the only female driver to win a title.
The Commission Internationale de Karting (CIK-FIA) was founded in 1962 by the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA).
The CIK-FIA was founded to govern the rising international sport of kart racing.
The inaugural CIK-FIA World Championship was hosted in 1964 at the Pista d'Oro in Rome.
The Pista d'Oro in Rome again held the CIK-FIA World Championship event in 1965.
The CIK-FIA began its homologation of distinct classes in the discipline in 1974.
The first 125 cc gearbox category, Formula C (FC), was created for the European Championship in 1974.
The 100 cc direct-drive category was clarified in 1976 with the introduction of Formula Europe.
Formula Europe was introduced to control technical evolutions and costs.
The direct-drive classes were adapted in 1981.

The 135 cc Formula K (FK), 100 cc Intercontinental A (ICA), and Junior Intercontinental A (ICA-J) were introduced to the World Championship, European Championship, and World Cup, respectively, in 1981.
By 2020, there were five CIK-FIA classes: OK, OK-Junior (OK-J), KZ, KZ2, and 60 Mini.
OK is the primary senior direct-drive CIK-FIA class.
OK-Junior (OK-J) is the under-15 direct-drive CIK-FIA class.
KZ is the primary gearbox CIK-FIA class.
KZ2 is the secondary gearbox CIK-FIA class.
60 Mini is the under-12 international CIK-FIA class.
Rotax was founded in 1920 as an internal combustion engine manufacturer.
Rotax entered the FK class in 1983.
Rotax founded the Rotax Max Challenge in 2000.
Italian American Motor Engineering (IAME) was founded as a kart manufacturer in 1968.
IAME was formed as a merger between Parilla and Komet.
IAME began operating its single-design championships, the IAME Series, in 2007.
The Switzerland-based RGMMC Group had been established in 2004.
RGMMC Group became the promoter of Rotax events in 2006.
RGMMC Group became the promoter of IAME events in 2016.
RGMMC Group became the promoter of CIK-FIA events in 2018.
Across 2018 and 2019, RGMMC promoted six World Championships, two World Cups, and eight European Championships with CIK-FIA.
COTF was founded in 2020 by the RGMMC Group to promote and develop four CIK-FIA classes: OK, OK-J, KZ2, and 60 Mini.
COTF's inaugural round at Wackersdorf on 7–10 May was delayed and cancelled amidst the COVID-19 pandemic in Europe.
The Kristianstad round on 25–28 June was also delayed and cancelled amidst the COVID-19 pandemic in Europe.
Zuera served as the debut circuit of the series on 16–19 July.
Over 170 drivers entered in preparation for the opening round of the European Championship that month.
The second and final round of COTF in 2020 was held on 1 November at Portimão in the OK and OK-J classes.
The Portimão round served as direct preparation for the World Championship one week later.
Nikita Bedrin was the inaugural OK champion in 2020.
Arvid Lindblad was the inaugural OK-J champion in 2020.
Paolo Ippolito was the inaugural KZ2 champion in 2020.
Dmitry Matveev was the inaugural 60 Mini champion in 2020.
The 2021 season was contested in OK and OK-J across three rounds at Genk, Zuera, and Campillos.
The Campillos round replaced the Franciacorta and Castelletto rounds, which were cancelled due to logistical challenges.
The Campillos round provided support for the upcoming World Championship.
Rafael Câmara claimed the OK championship in 2021.
Reigning World Champion Freddie Slater claimed the OK-J championship in 2021.
Prior to the 2022 season, the one-off Champions of the Future Winter Series was held at Franciacorta.
Tomass Štolcermanis won the OK class in the 2022 Champions of the Future Winter Series.
Maciej Gładysz won the OK-J class in the 2022 Champions of the Future Winter Series.
Simo Puhakka won the KZ2 class in the 2022 Champions of the Future Winter Series.
The regular season in 2022 was re-branded as the Champions of the Future Euro Series.
The 2022 Champions of the Future Euro Series was held over four rounds timetabled by factory-backed teams at Portimão, Zuera, Kristianstad, and Franciacorta.
British driver Joe Turney won the OK class in the 2022 Champions of the Future Euro Series.
British driver Nathan Tye won the OK-J class in the 2022 Champions of the Future Euro Series.
In 2023, COTF founded the Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA) in collaboration with F1 Academy.
COTFA in 2023 was a single-round event at Al Forsan.
The 2023 COTFA event at Al Forsan marked the series' first expansion beyond continental Europe.
The 2023 COTFA event included the recently established low-cost OK-National (OK-N) and OKN-Junior (OKN-J) classes, as well as 60 Mini.
F1 Academy sponsored the entries of three female drivers in each class in 2023.
Austin Gale was the inaugural OK-N winner in 2023.
James Anagnostiadis was the inaugural OKN-J winner in 2023.
Dan Allemann was the inaugural 60 Mini winner in 2023.
The five-round Euro Series in 2023 was held at Valencia, Třinec, Rødby, Cremona, and Franciacorta.
Each round of the 2023 Euro Series preceded rounds of the European and World Championships.
Alex Powell won in OK in the 2023 Euro Series.
Lewis Wherrell won in OK-J in the 2023 Euro Series.
The Třinec round in 2023 marked the first appearance of CIK-FIA competition in the Czech Republic since the 1990s.
With the creation of Champions of the Future Shifters in 2024, COTF expanded into all eight CIK-FIA classes: OK, OK-J, KZ, KZ2, KZ2-Masters (KZ2-M), OK-N, OKN-J, and 60 Mini.
The one-round Shifters championship at Portimão in 2024 was won by 2020 World Champion Jérémy Iglesias in KZ.
Daniel Vasile won in KZ2 in the 2024 Shifters championship.
Anthony Abbasse won in KZ2-M in the 2024 Shifters championship.
The Euro Series in 2024 was again held over five rounds at Valencia, Val d'Argenton, Slovakia, Kristianstad, and PF International.
Joe Turney won in OK for the second time in the 2024 Euro Series.
Dries Van Langendonck won in OK-J in the 2024 Euro Series.
The COTFA was expanded to six rounds in 2024, held at Cremona, Valencia, Franciacorta, Dubai, Al Ain, and Al Forsain.
Luna Fluxá won in OK-N in the 2024 COTFA.
Defending champion James Anagnostiadis won in OKN-J in the 2024 COTFA.
Priam Bruno won in 60 Mini in the 2024 COTFA.
Fluxá became the fifth woman in history to win a major senior international karting title.
Fluxá was the first woman to win a global championship since Susanna Raganelli in 1966.
The COTFA in 2024 used driver coaches from FIA Formula 2 and F1 Academy, including Isack Hadjar.
The COTFA in 2024 was used to scout driver talent by the Mercedes Junior Team and the Sauber Academy.
The Shifters series expanded to two rounds in 2025 at Valencia and Franciacorta.
Senna van Walstijn won in KZ in the 2025 Shifters series.
Maksim Orlov won in KZ2 in the 2025 Shifters series.
Angelo Lombardo won in KZ2-M in the 2025 Shifters series.
The 2025 Shifters event at Valencia was boycotted by 21 drivers, including six World Champions, in the KZ final due to a dispute with the CIK-FIA over its mandating Dunlop tyres.
19 of the 23 finalists withdrew or retired mid-race at the 2025 Shifters event at Valencia.
The CIK-FIA subsequently dropped Dunlop as a tyre supplier.
The five-round Euro Series in 2025 was claimed by two British drivers: reigning junior World Champion Kenzo Craigie (OK) and Noah Baglin (OK-J).
Noah Baglin overturned a 31-point deficit to William Calleja in the 2025 Euro Series.
Half of the OK-N entrants in COTFA in 2025 were female.
Markas Šilkūnas was victorious over Chiara Bättig across six rounds at Portimão, Valencia, Jesolo, Slovakia, Al Ain, and Al Forsan in the 2025 COTFA OK-N class.
Conor Clancy won in OKN-J in the 2025 COTFA.
Angelina Simons ended third in OKN-J in the 2025 COTFA.
Italian prodigy Niccoló Perico dominated in 60 Mini in the 2025 COTFA.
In 2026, COTFA is set to expand into the United Kingdom in collaboration with Motorsport UK, forming the four-round British Champions of the Future Academy Programme (British COTFA).
An Emirati title is due to be held across two rounds in November 2025 and February 2026 as another feeder series to the international COTFA.
A single-round Macanese title is due to be held at Coloane in January 2026.
F1 Academy is set to expand their support to nine drivers in both the British and Emirati series for a total of 27.
The Champions of the Future America Series (COTFAS) is set to debut across 10 rounds from January to September in 2026.
COTFAS will debut in partnership with K1 at K1 Circuit in California and Spring Mountain in Nevada.
The inaugural edition of COTF held four-day weekends.

The four-day weekends included free practice sessions on the Thursday and Friday mornings, qualifying practice on Friday afternoon, qualifying heats on Saturday and Sunday mornings, and pre-finals/finals on the Sunday afternoon.
The registration fees for the inaugural edition were €495 per round for 60 Mini.
The registration fees for the inaugural edition were €595 for OK, OK-J, and KZ2.
By 2024, the round fees increased to €675 for the Euro Series and Shifters.
An additional €100 charge for free practice was introduced by 2024.
The season fees for the arrive-and-drive Academy Program in 2024 were €29,000 for OK-N and OKN-J.
The season fees for the arrive-and-drive Academy Program in 2024 were €23,000 for 60 Mini.
The Academy Program season fees included a new chassis, engines, tyres, fuel, a paddock area, logistical support, travel, and accommodation.
As of 2025, the Euro Series is held over a three-day weekend.
The Euro Series weekend is composed of free practice (FP), time trials (TT), qualifying heats (QH), super heats (SH), and the finals.
On Thursday, the Euro Series schedule includes FP + TT in the morning and QH in the afternoon.
On Friday, the Euro Series schedule includes warm-up + QH.
On Saturday, the Euro Series schedule includes warm-up + SH in the morning, and OK-J and OK final in the afternoon.
The Euro Series follows the general CIK-FIA points system.
In the Euro Series, a maximum of 25 points is awarded for QH, 25 for SH, and 50 for finals.
Dead heats in finals are settled via count-back in the Euro Series.
As of 2025, Shifters is held over a three-day weekend.
The Shifters weekend is composed of free practice (FP), qualifying practice (QP), qualifying heats (QH), super heats (SH), and the finals.
On Thursday, the Shifters schedule includes FP in the morning and QP in the afternoon.
On Friday, the Shifters schedule includes warm-up + QH.
On Saturday, the Shifters schedule includes warm-up + SH in the morning, and KZ and KZ2 final in the afternoon.
Shifters follows the general CIK-FIA points system.
In Shifters, a maximum of 25 points is awarded for QH, 25 for SH, and 50 for finals.
Dead heats in finals are settled via count-back in Shifters.
As of 2025, the Academy Program is held over a three-day weekend.
The Academy Program weekend is composed of free practice (FP), qualifying practice (QP), qualifying heats (QH), and two finals in each class.
On Friday, the Academy Program schedule includes FP.
On Saturday, the Academy Program schedule includes FP + QP + QH in the morning, and OKN-J, 60 Mini, and OK-N final one in the afternoon.
On Sunday, the Academy Program schedule includes FP + QP + QH in the morning, and OKN-J, 60 Mini, and OK-N final two in the afternoon.
The Academy Program follows the general CIK-FIA points system.
In the Academy Program, a maximum of 25 points is awarded for QH and 50 for finals.
Dead heats in finals are settled via count-back in the Academy Program.
COTF exclusively operates on kart circuits with homologation from the CIK-FIA.
As of 2025, 18 circuits have appeared on the international COTF calendar.
Circuito Internacional de Zuera is located in Zuera, Spain, and appeared 3 times on the calendar from 2020–2022.
Kartódromo Internacional do Algarve is located in Portimão, Portugal, and appeared 5 times on the calendar from 2020–2025.
Karting Genk is located in Genk, Belgium, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2021.
Karting Campillos is located in Campillos, Spain, and appeared 2 times on the calendar from 2021–2025.
Franciacorta Karting Track is located in Bargnana, Italy, and appeared 5 times on the calendar from 2022–2025.
Åsum Ring is located in Kristianstad, Sweden, and appeared 3 times on the calendar from 2022–2025.
Kartodromo Internacional Lucas Guerrero is located in Valencia, Spain, and appeared 5 times on the calendar from 2023–2025.
Steel Ring Třinec is located in Třinec, Czech Republic, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2023.
Rødby Karting Ring is located in Rødbyhavn, Denmark, and appeared 2 times on the calendar from 2023–2025.
Cremona Karting is located in San Martino del Lago, Italy, and appeared 2 times on the calendar from 2023–2024.
Al Forsan International Sports Resort is located in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, and appeared 3 times on the calendar from 2023–2025.
Circuit du Val d'Argenton is located in Argentonnay, France, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2024.
Slovak Karting Center is located in Orechová Potôň, Slovakia, and appeared 2 times on the calendar from 2024–2025.
PF International Kart Circuit is located in Brandon, England, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2024.
Dubai Kartodrome is located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2024.
Al Ain Raceway is located in Al Ain, United Arab Emirates, and appeared 2 times on the calendar from 2024–2025.
Leopard Circuit Viterbo is located in Viterbo, Italy, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2025.
Pista Azzurra is located in Jesolo, Italy, and appeared 1 time on the calendar in 2025.
COTF is broadcast on YouTube and Motorsport.tv with live footage, commentary, and interviews for all competitive sessions.
The final round of the 2025 Shifters at Franciacorta had a record viewership of over 19 thousand people.
Over six thousand people watched the opening round of the 2024 Academy Program at Cremona.
Apex Timing provides live timing for each COTF event, including free practice and all competitive sessions, via their website.

In 2020, Nikita Bedrin (RUS) won the OK championship with a Tony Kart chassis and Vortex engine, achieving 1 win, 3 podiums, and 162 points (87.097% of achievable points), beating Joe Turney (GBR) by 4 points, with Rafael Câmara (BRA) in third place.

In 2021, Rafael Câmara (BRA) won the OK championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 1 win, 4 podiums, and 260 points (79.511% of achievable points), beating Arvid Lindblad (GBR) by 4 points, with Nikola Tsolov (BUL) in third place.

In 2022, Joe Turney (GBR) won the OK championship with a Tony Kart chassis and Vortex engine, achieving 2 wins, 3 podiums, and 92 points (66.667% of achievable points), beating Luigi Coluccio (ITA) by 10 points, with Tomass Štolcermanis (LAT) in third place.

In 2023, Alex Powell (JAM) won the OK championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 2 wins, 6 podiums, and 231 points (66.957% of achievable points), beating Kean Nakamura-Berta (GBR) by 19 points, with Joe Turney (GBR) in third place.

In 2024, Joe Turney (GBR) won his second OK championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 2 wins, 7 podiums, and 315 points (74.118% of achievable points), beating Thibaut Ramaekers (BEL) by 68 points, with Fionn McLaughlin (IRE) in third place.

In 2025, Kenzo Craigie (GBR) won the OK championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 2 wins, 7 podiums, and 333 points (78.353% of achievable points), beating Thibaut Ramaekers (BEL) by 56 points, with Christian Costoya (ESP) in third place.

In 2020, Arvid Lindblad (GBR) won the OK-Junior championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 1 win, 2 podiums, and 171 points (91.935% of achievable points), beating Ugo Ugochukwu (USA) by 4 points, with Freddie Slater (GBR) in third place.

In 2021, Freddie Slater (GBR) won the OK-Junior championship with a Kosmic chassis and Vortex engine, achieving 2 wins, 2 podiums, and 249 points (76.147% of achievable points), beating Kirill Kutskov (RUS) by 7 points, with Maksimilian Popov (RUS) in third place.

In 2022, Nathan Tye (GBR) won the OK-Junior championship with a Sodi chassis and TM engine, achieving 3 wins, 7 podiums, and 124 points (89.855% of achievable points), beating Anatoly Khavalkin by 37 points, with Dmitry Matveev (ITA) in third place.

In 2023, Lewis Wherrell (GBR) won the OK-Junior championship with an Exprit chassis and TM engine, achieving 5 wins, 8 podiums, and 243 points (70.435% of achievable points), beating Dries Van Langendonck (BEL) by 51 points, with Thibaut Ramaekers (BEL) in third place.

In 2024, Dries Van Langendonck (BEL) won the OK-Junior championship with an Exprit chassis and TM engine, achieving 5 wins, 7 podiums, and 257 points (60.471% of achievable points), beating Niklas Schaufler (AUT) by 20 points, with Kenzo Craigie (GBR) in third place.

In 2025, Noah Baglin (GBR) won the OK-Junior championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 4 wins, 6 podiums, and 309 points (72.706% of achievable points), beating William Calleja (AUS) by 73 points, with Ilie Tristan Crisan (CAN) in third place.

In 2020, Paolo Ippolito (ITA) won the KZ2 championship with a CRG chassis and TM engine, achieving 1 win, 2 podiums, and 87 points (97.753% of achievable points), beating Antonio Garay Salinas (ESP) by 4 points, with Brice de Gaye (FRA) in third place.

In 2020, Dmitry Matveev (RUS) won the 60 Mini championship with an Energy Corse chassis and TM engine, achieving 2 wins, 2 podiums, and 89 points (100.000% of achievable points), beating Kean Nakamura-Berta (JPN) by 4 points, with Mark Kastelic (SVN) in third place.

In 2023, Austin Gale (THA) won the OK-National championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 0 wins, 2 podiums, and 48 points (77.419% of achievable points), beating Peter Stiller (ITA) by 2 points, with Suleiman Zanfari (MAR) in third place.

In 2024, Luna Fluxá (ESP) won the OK-National championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 10 wins, 17 podiums, and 665 points (87.500% of achievable points), beating Markas Šilkūnas (LIT) by 125 points, with Hugo Herrouin (FRA) in third place.

In 2025, Markas Šilkūnas (LIT) won the OK-National championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 13 wins, 18 podiums, and 696 points (91.579% of achievable points), beating Chiara Bättig (SUI) by 149 points, with Wojciech Woda (POL) in third place.

In 2023, James Anagnostiadis (AUS) won the OKN-Junior championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 1 win, 2 podiums, and 52 points (83.871% of achievable points), beating Conor Clancy (UAE) by 0 points, with Kaiden Higgins (AUS) in third place.

In 2024, James Anagnostiadis (AUS) won his second OKN-Junior championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 12 wins, 18 podiums, and 674 points (88.684% of achievable points), beating William Marshall (RSA) by 174 points, with Toby Gale (THA) in third place.

In 2025, Conor Clancy (UAE) won the OKN-Junior championship with a Kart Republic chassis and IAME engine, achieving 6 wins, 12 podiums, and 519 points (68.289% of achievable points), beating Many Nuvolini (FRA) by 84 points, with Angelina Simons (ESP) in third place.

In 2023, Dan Allemann (SUI) won the 60 Mini championship with a Parolin chassis and TM engine, achieving 2 wins, 2 podiums, and 61 points (98.387% of achievable points), beating Priam Bruno (BEL) by 9 points, with Leonidas Peruzzi (UAE) in third place.

In 2024, Priam Bruno (BEL) won the 60 Mini championship with a Parolin chassis and TM engine, achieving 9 wins, 15 podiums, and 664 points (87.368% of achievable points), beating Niccoló Perico (ITA) by 102 points, with Albert Tamm (EST) in third place.
In 2024, Niccoló Perico (ITA) was the U10 Champion in 60 Mini.

In 2025, Niccoló Perico (ITA) won the 60 Mini championship with a Parolin chassis and TM engine, achieving 11 wins, 14 podiums, and 644 points (84.737% of achievable points), beating Wynn Godschalk (USA) by 124 points, with Zayne Burgess (USA) in third place.
In 2025, Wynn Godschalk (USA) was the U10 Champion in 60 Mini.
In 2024, Jérémy Iglesias (FRA) won the KZ championship with a CRG chassis and TM engine, achieving 1 win and 1 podium, beating Senna van Walstijn (NED), with Pedro Hiltbrand (ESP) in third place.

In 2025, Senna van Walstijn (NED) won the KZ championship with a Sodi chassis and TM engine, achieving 0 wins, 4 podiums, and 163 points (81.500% of achievable points), beating Jean Nomblot (FRA) by 25 points, with Giuseppe Palomba (ITA) in third place.
In 2024, Daniel Vasile (ROM) won the KZ2 championship with a Birel ART chassis and TM engine, achieving 1 win and 1 podium, beating Markus Kajak (EST), with Artem Severiukhin (ARM) in third place.

In 2025, Maksim Orlov (white) won the KZ2 championship with a Sodi chassis and TM engine, achieving 3 wins, 5 podiums, and 180 points (90.000% of achievable points), beating Max Schleimer (GER) by 62 points, with Kasper Schormans (NED) in third place.
In 2024, Anthony Abbasse (FRA) won the KZ2-Masters championship with a Sodi chassis and TM engine, achieving 1 win and 1 podium, beating André Nicastro (BRA), with Daniel Bray (NZL) in third place.

In 2025, Angelo Lombardo (ITA) won the KZ2-Masters championship with a Maranello chassis and TM engine, achieving 1 win and 1 podium, beating Davide Forè (ITA), with Riccardo Nalon (ITA) in third place.
The Champions of the Future Academy Program Macau (COTFA Macau) is the national championship of Macau sanctioned by the Automobile General Association Macao-China (AAMC).
COTFA Macau is set to debut in 2026 at Coloane.
The Champions of the Future Academy Program UAE (COTFA UAE) is the national championship of the United Arab Emirates sanctioned by the Emirates Motorsports Organization (EMSO).
COTFA UAE is set to debut across two rounds in 2025 and 2026 at Al Forsan.
The British Champions of the Future Academy Programme (British COTFA) is the national championship of the United Kingdom sanctioned by Motorsport UK.
British COTFA is set to debut across eight rounds in 2026 at Silverstone, PF International, Larkhall, and Whilton Mill.
The Champions of the Future American Series (COTFAS) is the national championship of the United States sanctioned by K1.
COTFAS is set to debut across 10 rounds in 2026 at K1 Circuit and Spring Mountain.
The Champions of the Future Winter Series, also known simply as the Winter Series, was held as a one-off event at Franciacorta on 24–27 February 2022.
In the 2022 Winter Series, Tomass Štolcermanis (LAT) won the OK class with an Energy Corse chassis and TM engine, beating Matheus Ferreira (BRA), with Kean Nakamura-Berta (GBR) in third place.
In the 2022 Winter Series, Maciej Gładysz (POL) won the OK-J class with an LN Kart chassis and Vortex engine, beating Andrés Cárdenas (PER), with Anatoly Khavalkin (RUS) in third place.
In the 2022 Winter Series, Simo Puhakka (FIN) won the KZ2 class with a Tony Kart chassis and Vortex engine, beating Giuseppe Palomba (ITA), with David Liwinski (POL) in third place.
In August 2025, RGMMC—in partnership with its sister company Motorsport Performance Academy—announced the creation of the Champions of the Future Racing Academy.
The Champions of the Future Racing Academy is a year-long driver development programme led by Augusto Farfus.
The Champions of the Future Racing Academy includes extensive Formula 4 testing for drivers in their final season of kart racing.
The COTFA champions will additionally receive test sessions.
The OK-N champion will receive an F4 test.
The OKN-J champion will receive a legends car test.
